_strings.@@cb1b6c872f96: Treaty conformity — NJ does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by NJ. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: New Jersey does NOT start from federal AGI. The NJ Gross Income Tax is a self-contained system that builds gross income from its own statutory categories. The 2024 NJ-1040 instructions explicitly direct: "Use 'State Wages' from box 16 of your W-2, not federal wages (box 1)" and note that New Jersey's inclusion rules (e.g. 401(k) is the only pre-tax plan excluded) "cause your State wages (box 16) to be higher than your federal wages (box 1)"; income taxable for NJ that is not in box 16 "must [be] add[ed] ... back into your State wages." Because NJ never imports federal AGI, a federal tax-treaty exemption (which reduces federal box 1 / federal AGI) does NOT automatically pass through. The word "treaty" does not appear anywhere in the 2024 NJ-1040 instructions, and NJ's Gross Income Tax Act contains no provision recognizing federal income tax treaties, so federally treaty-exempt wages are generally still taxable for NJ purposes. This puts NJ in the "builds income from scratch, no treaty pass-through" category -> conforms_to_federal_treaties = false. (Conservative reading; the precise NJ treatment of a specific treaty article should be confirmed at the DOR.)

This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form NJ-1040 Line 29, New Jersey Gross Income (Line 27 total income minus Line 28c pension/retirement exclusion). NJ never starts from federal AGI — gross income is built from NJ's own categories (wages from W-2 box 16 State wages). The op subtracts $1,000 x exemptions_count (Line 6 regular exemptions: self, spouse/CU partner, or registered domestic partner) and $1,500 x dependents_count (Line 10 qualified dependent children plus Line 11 other dependents) to approximate Line 42 New Jersey Taxable Income. If any UNMODELED subtraction applies — Line 7 senior 65+ ($1,000 each), Line 8 blind/disabled ($1,000 each), Line 9 veteran ($6,000 each), Line 12 dependent attending college ($1,000 each), Lines 31-37c deductions (medical over 2% of gross income, alimony, qualified conservation, health enterprise zone, alternative business calculation, organ/bone marrow donation, NJBEST up to $10,000, NJCLASS up to $2,500, tuition up to $10,000), or the Line 41 Property Tax Deduction (up to $15,000; $7,500 MFS) — reduce the supplied base by those amounts too, or compute on the form; otherwise the result will overstate Line 43. Adjudication note (two-pass): the 2024 Tables A and B were drafted from the resident booklet (p.63) and re-verified against the 2024 NJ-1040NR instructions (p.43) — identical schedules, and NJ's brackets are statutory (unchanged since the 2020 millionaire's-tax addition; 2024 print matches 2023 exactly). All printed STEP 3 subtraction constants were reconciled against exact cumulative bracket math: every constant is exact EXCEPT Table B's -$1,154.50 (see the misprint note). Tax Table MANDATE below $100,000: Line 43 directs 'If the income on line 42 is less than $100,000, use the Tax Table on page 54. Otherwise, calculate the tax by using the Tax Rate Schedules on page 63.' Bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands; the filed form must use the table below $100,000. The Tax Rate Schedules (shipped here) govern at $100,000 and above. Filing threshold = no tax due: you are not required to file (and owe no NJ tax) if New Jersey gross income (Line 29) is at or below $10,000 (single; married/CU partner filing separate) or $20,000 (married/CU couple filing joint; head of household; qualifying widow(er)/surviving CU partner). NOT modeled — the brackets tax from the first dollar, so below-threshold filers would be overstated; file only to recover withholding or refundable credits. Printed-constant divergence (Table B only), the famous misprint constant: the 70,000-80,000 bracket prints 'multiply by .035, subtract $1,154.50', but the exact cumulative constant is $1,155.00 — the printed schedule yields $0.50 MORE than exact marginal-bracket math everywhere inside that bracket, and rejoins exactly at $80,000 (the next constant, $2,775.00, is exact). Every other printed constant in Tables A and B equals the cumulative sum exactly. The same $1,154.50 appears in both the 2024 resident (p.63) and nonresident (p.43) prints, as it has since 2020. One schedule covers three statuses: Table B applies identically to married/CU couple filing joint, head of household, and qualifying widow(er)/surviving CU partner — the head_of_household brackets shipped here are Table B, identical to married_filing_jointly, and the engine's QSS->married_filing_jointly mapping is exact (no divergence). Table A applies to single and married/CU partner filing separate (MFS is NOT half of MFJ; copied as printed). Civil-union partners must use the corresponding married/CU filing statuses. New Jersey has NO standard deduction — standard_deduction is null because none exists, not because it is income-dependent. NJ instead allows specific deductions on Lines 31-37c (medical expenses over 2% of gross income, alimony, qualified conservation contribution, health enterprise zone, alternative business calculation adjustment, organ/bone marrow donation, up to $10,000 NJBEST 529 contributions, up to $2,500 NJCLASS loan principal and interest, up to $10,000 tuition) and the Line 41 Property Tax Deduction (property taxes paid or 18% of rent, capped at $15,000; $7,500 if married/CU partner filing separately). None of these are modeled. The op applies ONLY the $1,000 Line 6 regular exemption (x exemptions_count) and the $1,500 Line 10/11 dependent exemption (x dependents_count). The result equals Form NJ-1040 Line 43 only when no other exemption (senior, blind/disabled, veteran, college dependent) and no Lines 31-37c or Line 41 deduction applies; otherwise pre-subtract those amounts from the base you supply. NJ exemptions are genuine BASE reductions (Line 13 total -> Line 30, subtracted from gross income before the rates), not credits. Separately, NJ's refundable CREDITS are not modeled: NJ Earned Income Tax Credit (Line 58, 40% of federal EIC; $253 fixed amount for 2024 age-expansion filers), $50 Property Tax Credit (Line 56; $25 MFS), Child and Dependent Care Credit (Line 64, Worksheet J), NJ Child Tax Credit (Line 65, up to $1,000 per child age 5 or younger), and the Credit for Income Taxes Paid to Other Jurisdictions (Line 44). Part-year residents must prorate the Line 13 exemption total on Line 30 by months of NJ residency (15+ days counts as a month) — NOT modeled; full-year exemption amounts are shipped. No 2024 rate change: the 2024 schedules (top rate 10.75% over $1,000,000) are the statutory schedules in force since tax year 2020, republished unchanged in the final 2024 booklet used for the 2025 filing season; New Jersey had no mid-year retroactive rate legislation for 2024.
